title: How to Do Influencer Marketing on a Budget (2026 Guide for Small Brands)
excerpt: A practical guide for small and growing brands: how to run influencer marketing on a budget with micro creators, gifting, UGC and performance-based pay.
content:
How do you do influencer marketing on a budget?

Quick answer: work with micro and nano creators instead of big names, start with product gifting and UGC, pay for results (views, sales or posts delivered) rather than flat upfront fees where you can, and turn the videos that perform into ads. You don't need an agency to start: a clear brief, a short list of creators in your niche and a simple tracking sheet are enough to run your first campaign.

1. Work with micro and nano creators

Creators with roughly 1,000 to 100,000 followers usually charge far less than large accounts, reply to brands faster, and often have audiences that trust their recommendations. For a small budget, several small creators also spread your risk: if one video flops, others may not. See what a micro-influencer is.

2. Start with product gifting

Sending free product to creators who genuinely fit your niche is the cheapest way to start. Your cost is product and shipping. Two things make gifting work:

  • Pick creators who already post in your category, so the product fits their content.
  • Be clear about what you hope for (for example one post or video) while accepting that gifting usually isn't guaranteed. Not every gifted creator posts, so ship to more creators than the number of posts you need.

3. Buy UGC instead of reach

UGC (user-generated content) means paying creators for the video itself, which you then post or run as ads. You get content that looks native to TikTok and Instagram without paying for a creator's audience. It's often the best value when you plan to run paid social anyway.

4. Pay for results, not promises

Flat fees paid upfront are the riskiest spend on a small budget. Lower-risk options:

ModelYou pay forGood for
Affiliate / commissionSales through a creator's code or linkProducts with clear online checkout
Pay per viewViews the creator's post actually reachesAwareness and testing hooks
Per-video UGCEach finished videoAd creative
GiftingProduct and shippingFirst campaigns, product seeding

5. Write a one-page brief

Good briefs save money because creators get it right the first time. Include: what the product does in one sentence, the one feeling or result to show, two or three hooks that work in your category, must-say and must-avoid points, deliverables, deadline, and disclosure requirements.

6. Reuse the winners as ads

The biggest saving comes after the post. Ask for usage rights up front, then put budget behind the videos that already performed organically, through TikTok Spark Ads or Instagram/Facebook partnership ads. You stop paying to test creative that doesn't work.

7. Track the basics

For each creator, track cost, posts delivered, views, clicks or code uses, and which hook they used. After two or three rounds you'll know which creators, hooks and formats to repeat.

Do you need an influencer marketing agency?

Not to start. Agencies help when you need scale, legal contracts across many creators, or strategy you can't do in-house, but retainers can use up a small budget before any content goes live. Most small brands are better off running a few campaigns themselves first.

Common budget mistakes

  • Paying one big creator instead of testing several small ones.
  • Paying flat fees without usage rights, so you can't reuse the best video as an ad.
  • Choosing creators by follower count instead of content quality and niche fit.
  • Skipping disclosure: creators must label paid or gifted posts.

Pay only for the views you get

Newcollab offers performance UGC for DTC brands: creators in your niche post about your product on their own TikTok or Instagram, and you pay a rate per 1,000 views that you set, with caps per video and per month. Campaigns start from $300, you can pause anytime, and you can boost the best posts as ads.

faq.question: How much should a small brand spend on influencer marketing?
faq.answer: Start with what you can afford to test: product for a gifting round, a few paid UGC videos, or a capped performance campaign. Spread it across several small creators, measure results, and put more budget behind what works.

faq.question: Is influencer marketing worth it for small businesses?
faq.answer: It can be, especially with micro creators, gifting and UGC, because costs are low and the content can be reused as ads. The key is choosing creators who fit your niche and tracking results so you repeat what works.

faq.question: How do you find influencers on a budget?
faq.answer: Look at who already posts in your category on TikTok and Instagram, check creators tagging similar brands, invite customers who create content, and use creator platforms that let creators apply to your campaign.

faq.question: What is cheaper, influencers or UGC?
faq.answer: UGC is often cheaper per video because you pay for the content, not the creator's audience. Influencer posts add organic reach on the creator's account. Many brands combine both: creators post organically and the best videos become ads.

faq.question: Do gifted influencer posts need to be disclosed?
faq.answer: Yes. In the US the FTC expects creators to disclose free products as well as paid deals, using the platform's paid partnership label or a clear #ad.
